## What you need to do

- **Docker nodes: recreate them once.** This release's server image is **system level 2** (a new browser base, with the fix for the VNC desktop after a restart). A node still on an older image refuses the level-2 server update until it is recreated. Run

  ```bash
  autobyteus-docker upgrade --all
  ```

  Each node keeps its track and its volumes and data: nodes on the stable track (the default) get 1.5.14, and nodes on the beta track get it too and stay on the beta track. Updating in place with `autobyteus-docker update --all` works only for nodes that already run a level-2 image.
- **Saved organization runs are converted on the first start, once, and this cannot be undone.** An organization run is now a container of runs, and your saved organization runs are converted to that shape: their conversations, messages, memory, Tasks and history are kept, and the files an organization's agent received from another node, or attached to messages and Tasks, still open. **After updating, do not go back to 1.5.13 or older; if you need to go back, contact support instead of installing an older version.**
- **Update the desktop app, the phone app and every node you connect to together.** That means every Docker node, every node on another computer and every paired node. Several things in this release changed what the app and the nodes say to each other:
  - A message's reference file opens from the node that holds the message, so an app and a node of different versions cannot open each other's reference files.
  - A conversation now shows only the times the node recorded, so an app on this release does not accept a live update from an earlier node.
  - A message, a delegation or a Task close between two paired nodes is refused when one of them is on an older release, and agents on another node are addressed by their run ID and the node's name.
  - The agent pages, the Memory page and the connection's resend of its state changed shape.
- **Two built-in agents are removed on the first start: the Skill Self-Evolver and the Memory Compactor.** Their installed agent folders are deleted and no copy is kept; your other agents, every run and its history (the old Memory Compactor runs too) and all memory files stay as they are. If a Team or Org you made lists one of them as a member, replace that member, because its definition is gone. If you want a copy of the two agents, back up your agents folder before you update.
- **Nothing else to do, and three things happen once on their own:** the app converts the stored links of files attached to delegated runs (it keeps a copy first; on a very large data folder this takes about half a minute), your Work Journals are rendered again once in the background while memory search re-indexes them (no data is lost), and the converted organization runs above.
- **iPhone and iPad: update AutoByteus from TestFlight** to the newest build of version 1.5.14. It is a TestFlight release only; nothing is sent for App Store review.
- **Android:** install this release's APK (`AutoByteus_personal_android-1.5.14-release.apk`) so the app matches your nodes.
- **Ubuntu desktop (AppImage): allow the one-time setup.** On Ubuntu desktops that restrict the browser sandbox, opening the new AppImage offers a protected installation. It needs an internet connection and one Ubuntu administrator authorization the first time. Afterwards open AutoByteus from the menu. Do not turn the sandbox off to get around a setup message; follow the recovery message instead.
- **Desktop installs on the beta track** that already have a 1.5.14 beta are offered this release as an update too.

## Good To Know

- **This release cannot be rolled back after the first start** (see the organization conversion above). The two removed built-in agents do not come back.
- **A trusted run workspace can change how a Grok run behaves.** To show a workspace's skills, AutoByteus starts each Grok run with that run's workspace trusted, for that run only, and saves nothing in your Grok settings. As with trusted folders in Grok itself, Grok then also loads that workspace's own Grok hooks, MCP and LSP servers, instructions and permission rules.
- Every message to an agent on another node now names the node: `send_message_to` needs `node` together with the run ID, also for a run it delegated to; `delegate_task` to an existing copy on another node needs `node` too.
- A run that has delegated work now opens on **Activity**, like every other run. Its messages are on the **Messages** tab.
- **The conversation keeps its order, and every time on it is the node's.** The "last activity" time in the run list still follows the clock of the device you look at it with. The time of a reopened message is the moment the node saved it, which can differ by a few thousandths of a second from the time it showed live; the order is the same.
- The Work Journal skips Antigravity's reads of its own tool files and shows what its tool calls did, for new work only: runs that already finished keep the short size-only text that was recorded at the time.
- A stopped call keeps the error text "Tool execution interrupted." in its details; a tool call that was interrupted shows "Unknown" on the phone, as it already did on the desktop. On the phone, a relative link inside a workspace Markdown file you open from Files still does not open the linked file, and the phone downloads a video or audio file completely before it plays.
- After you switch a run's agent runtime, the new Claude agent in our checks read the start and the end of a very long journal (about 2,400 lines) and skipped the middle; Codex and AutoByteus agents read it to the end.
- Semantic memory is on for every agent, with no switch.
- A message that does not get through to an agent comes back to the message box, and when the app cannot tell whether it arrived, the message may still appear in the conversation: check before you send it again.
- Files an agent sends to another node are limited per file (2 GiB by default; change it with `AUTOBYTEUS_RECEIVED_FILE_MAX_MB`, 1 to 4096 MiB) and 4 GiB per call.
- Application packages still import public GitHub repositories only.
- A DeepSeek agent that never starts now fails after 90 seconds instead of 15.

## What's New

- **Organizations are containers of runs.** Each team in an organization is a team run of its own, and each organization agent an agent run of its own, with its own run, memory and messages, so team features work the same inside and outside organizations. The organization still looks and works as one in the app (one launch page, one view, one Stop and reopen).
- **Teams and organizations follow their definitions while they run.** Add a member, remove one, change the coordinator or the handoff rules (in the app or in the agent package's files), and the running team follows: a new member joins Offline and starts when it is needed, a removed member finishes its current turn (its row is tagged **Leaving**), and the other members are told what changed. Mounting a team or adding an agent adds it to the running organization; removing one lets it finish, then removes it, keeping its history. A stopped team picks up the changes when you open it again.
- **Agents can find and message any running agent.** A new tool, `list_running_agents`, lists the agents and teams a person started that are running now, on this node or a paired node; select it in an agent's tool list to give it to that agent. `send_message_to` reaches any running agent by its run ID (on a paired node with the node's name), including task agents and members of a Team or Org. A message never wakes or restarts anything.
- **Agents can send files to agents on other nodes.** `send_message_to` and `delegate_task` with reference files now work between nodes: the files are copied to the receiving node, which keeps its own read-only copy under `received_files/`, checked by size and SHA-256, and a broken transfer resumes where it stopped. A saved Task can be given to another node with its context files.
- **Closing a Task stops the work it delegated to another node**, within seconds, including a team member in the middle of a turn; if the other node is offline the stop is sent when it can be reached again. Reopening the Task and messaging the run continues it.
- **Every agent run has a Messages list**: a **Messages** tab on the desktop and **Messages** in the run's ⋮ menu on the phone, with every message the run's agent sent or received, from task agents, other runs and other nodes (named with a node chip), 50 at a time with **Load more**, live and after a reload. A reference file attached to a message opens from whichever run holds that message, for delegated agents and teams too, and the viewer says why when a file cannot be opened.
- **Semantic memory for every agent, and a new Memory page.** Every agent, in every runtime and every kind of run, gets its own folder of reusable knowledge, plus one global folder that every agent can read and write. The Memory page is organized by owner (**Global · Agents · Agent Teams · Agent Orgs**), shows an agent's episodic memory (all its runs, with a filter) and its semantic folder, and lists a Team inside an Org under its Org. The folders open read-only, like the Skills page.
- **Continue a stopped run on another model.** A stopped AutoByteus run whose model is gone (for example one you removed from LM Studio) can continue on another model: open the run's Settings, choose any model the list offers and Save. Your next message starts a fresh session on the new model, which continues from the run's work journal; this also applies to a model with a smaller or unknown context window.
- **A lost runtime session is renewed.** Claude Code deletes saved sessions after 30 days, and every message to such a run used to fail. Now the run continues in a new session of the same runtime and model, the chat says so, and the new agent is told which work journal to read. It works on every runtime that keeps a saved session.
- **Switching a run's agent runtime tells the new agent which work journal to read first**, and to read it completely.
- **A message is never lost silently.** A message you send always reaches the agent, or comes back to the message box with a notice saying why, for single agents, Team and Org members, delegated agents and agents on a paired node, on the desktop and the phone.
- **Stop is quiet when there is nothing to stop.** Pressing Stop twice, or after the agent finished, no longer shows an error; the button shows "Stopping…", and a real failure shows one plain message that names the agent.
- **A conversation keeps its order, and every time on it is the node's.** Your message always shows before the notice and the reply, whatever your clock says; a platform notice sits right after its message when you reopen a run; the time on a message, a notice, a tool call or a compaction row is the time the node recorded, so a device with the wrong clock shows the same times as any other.
- **Platform notices get their own light row** ("Application restarted", "Background tasks finished", "Skill updated", "Tools updated", "Agent runtime changed") with an icon and a label, never inside the agent's message.
- **A tool call you stopped says "Stopped"**, with a stop icon, in the conversation, the Activity panel and on the phone, live and after you reopen the run, for every runtime. The tasks of a stopped run end as "Stopped: the run ended".
- **Links in chat can point to a file in the run's folder.** A link such as `[clip](media/clip.mp4)` that an agent writes opens that file from the agent's own folder, on the desktop and the phone. In the Files panel, a relative link in a Markdown file opens the linked file in a preview tab.
- **Private GitHub repositories for agent packages and skills.** You can import a private GitHub repository as an agent package or a skill source with the node's GitHub token. When GitHub cannot see the repository, the import box says it is private or not found and offers **Connect GitHub** right there: paste a token and Save. The import areas show a **GitHub connection** line with **Connect GitHub**, **Replace token** and **Disconnect**. Update checks and updates of a private package or skill source work like a public one, including automatic updates. The token is checked with GitHub when you save it, kept in the node's secret vault, never shown again, and sent only to GitHub, as a request header. A Docker node has its own connection. Create a fine-grained token with **Repository permissions → Contents: Read-only** for only the repositories you need; it is the same token the GitHub integration uses.
- **Grok starts reliably, offers the right models and shows its own turns.** AutoByteus waits up to 90 seconds for Grok to start on a busy computer, and up to 3 seconds for Grok to announce its real model list instead of offering its older built-in models (reading the Grok model list and starting a Grok run take about 3 seconds longer). Grok agents see their workspace's skills. When a background command of a Grok agent ends and Grok starts a turn of its own, the run shows it (a notice, then the reasoning, text, tool calls and usage), holds your message until it ends, and Stop cancels it.
- **The Work Journal shows what Antigravity's tool calls did.** A file read shows the lines that were read, a failed command shows its exit code as `exit N`, and file writes and edits show their full content and diff, also when Antigravity made several calls in one response; memory search can find them. Antigravity's reads of its own tool files and its long saved outputs are summarized instead of cluttering the journal.
- **Antigravity background tasks stay listed after they end** (with their exit code, or "Stopped: the run ended") when you open or reload the Activity tab.
- **Phone: a built-in demo and a new start screen (iPhone and iPad).** The first screen has **Try demo**, which opens the whole app with sample agents, teams and files, with no account, no computer and no network. It has the same start screen as the Android app (Scan, Your nodes, Other ways to connect), accepts a shared pairing link, shows run list and open run side by side on a wide iPad, and **Download** opens the share sheet. The app icon is now the AutoByteus logo, and the app is built with Xcode 27 and the iOS 27 SDK.
- **Phone: Activity shows what each tool did.** A tool call shows the command it ran, the file it touched, the query, the recipient or the Task, with a clear status that never relies on color alone; tap a call to open its details full screen, updating while you watch. Memory compactions open too, and a background task unfolds to show its full command and how it ended. The desktop uses the same wording.
- **Ubuntu desktop (AppImage):** a protected one-time installation on desktops that restrict the browser sandbox, the app's own icon and window grouping in the Dock, and, when **Update automatically** is on, a verified update installs right away (a running turn can be interrupted; the run gets an update notice and you can continue).
- **Claude agents can run a shell command for up to 2 hours**, and the Background Tasks panel says in one line why a task ended (a time limit, low memory, the run ended, or the exit code).
- **Smaller downloads.** The desktop apps and the Docker server package no longer include a copy of Claude Code that was never used (about 75 to 190 MB smaller per platform); Claude agents keep using the Claude Code you installed.

## Improvements

- A run whose saved model its runtime no longer offers is refused when it starts, with a message that names the model and says what to do; Settings marks each team member whose saved model is affected. Refusal messages now say what happened, why and what to do next.
- A team's token total counts only that team's runs.
- Workspace choices (when you start a chat, change Run Settings, or on the phone's launch picker) offer only your folders and the temporary workspace, not a skill's folder.
- When the availability check of the Grok Build or Antigravity runtime is slow because the computer is busy, the app reports that it timed out instead of "Grok CLI version or agent mode is unsupported".
- The Files viewer shows an error state with the node's message for a file it cannot give you, instead of the raw refusal text; a file whose own text is `{"error":…}` opens as the text it is.
- The earlier-events page shows the same tool-card summary and "Stopped" status as the live conversation.
- After you send a message, the conversation moves to it and follows the reply, also when you had scrolled up.
- On the phone, artifacts are read only and the icons are part of the app, so they show without an internet connection.
- Releases now check every Linux AppImage on a clean system image before they are published.

## Fixes

- The Linux ARM64 AppImage starts on a standard desktop again, with no extra system package (it no longer needs `zlib1g-dev` or `libfuse2`).
- Antigravity is no longer reported as unavailable when its CLI is slow to start on a busy computer: the app waits up to 10 seconds for the CLI's first answer and up to 30 seconds for its model list.
- Agents with very long IDs no longer fail to start for lack of a memory folder.
- Videos and audio in chat play on the phone with a clear loading state ("Loading video…" with how much has arrived) and a plain message with **Retry** when a file cannot be loaded, instead of "Video URL is not available." while a file loads.
- Files open right after a node restart.
- The Windows desktop build no longer leaves a staging folder inside the package.

## Upgrade Notes

- **Docker.** The server image is `autobyteus/autobyteus-server:1.5.14`; `:latest` and `:beta` both point to it, at system level 2. Run `autobyteus-docker upgrade --all` once (see above). Beta-track nodes stay on the beta track with a plain `autobyteus-docker upgrade --all`; `autobyteus-docker upgrade --all --tag latest` returns them to stable, which is safe now because this release is at least as new as every 1.5.14 beta.
- **Desktop.** Installs on the beta track that already have a 1.5.14 beta are offered this release as an update too; installs on the stable track are offered it as the new stable.
